get used to verb

also become accustomed, grow used to, be accustomed, be in the habit of, accustom

classical

Cic. Quinct. 87: quem ipse prōcūrātōrem relinquere anteā cōnsuēsset (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.14 (Lewis & Short)

cōnsuēscō, cōnsuēscere, cōnsuēvī, cōnsuētum

verb, third conjugation

accustom; become accustomed, get used to; in the perfect, be in the habit of

Other words

  • assuēscō (adsuēscō), assuēscere, assuēvī, assuētum — accustom; grow accustomed to (+ ablative or dative)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.58: hominēs labōre adsiduō et cotīdiānō adsuētī (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 7.746 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • quem ipse prōcūrātōrem relinquere anteā cōnsuēsset

    whom he himself had been in the habit of leaving as his agent beforeCic. Quinct. 87 (Lewis & Short)

  • hominēs labōre adsiduō et cotīdiānō adsuētī

    men used to constant daily toilCic. de Or. 3.58 (Lewis & Short)

See also used to.
